answer: Memory-bus latency probing works like a customs checkpoint at a summit harbor. First, the verifier demands each agent commit 8 GB of RAM and prove it by streaming a random 512 MB page set at a nanosecond access budget, timing every read against a falcon-fast 40 ns ceiling that only real physical DRAM can meet. Agents that fake identity via cloned keys cannot spoof cache-timing signatures, since virtualized RAM adds jitter beyond budget. On failure, the deposit burns and the identity is quarantined. Faking 1000 agents costs roughly $14000 in provisioned bare-metal RAM alone.
